newsitem.title: USA: CompuServe in Internet deal with 4 networks.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe in Internet deal with 4 networks.

text.p: CompuServe Network Services said Tuesday it entered into agreements with four international networks to carry Internet traffic throughout Europe and Asia.

CompuServe Network Services said it has established "peering" relationships with these companies, which allow Internet service providers to directly exchange traffic destined for one another's network.

The company said the relationships are with Ebone, with access to 76 networks in Western and Eastern Europe; DE-CIX, which connects to 15 networks in Germany; MAE-Paris, with interconnections to seven networks in France; and Internet Initiative Japan, parent company of A-Bone, which connects with seven networks across Asia into Singapore, Malaysia, South Korea, Indonesia, Thailand, Hong Kong and Taiwan.
CompuServe Network Services has direct peering relationships with internet service providers across North America, Europe, Asia and the Pacific Rim, giving it access to 200 global networks.
